Three years ago, I sold my house in Chicago and moved to a small town in Portugal. People ask me if I miss home. Honestly, not much. If I still lived in Chicago, I would be shoveling snow right now. I would pay three times more for everything, and I would spend my evenings in front of the TV. Here, I walk to the market and I know everybody. If I had to choose again, I would do exactly the same thing. My only problem is my family. I wish my grandkids lived closer. But that is what airplanes are for.

My friends keep asking me why I do not move to Europe. I have a passport, I have the money, and I love to travel. But if I moved, I would lose the most important thing I have: my people. Here, if I called a friend at midnight, she would come. In a new country, who would I call? I wish the weather were cooler in the summer, and I wish the traffic were better. But if I lived anywhere else, I would miss my Sunday lunches every single week. For me, travel is for visiting. Home is where your people are.
